messages.subject: Accumulating random renamed R files
parts:
Hello this post is in regards to the method outlined here:
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/wiki/Using-rhipe-on-a-cluster--without--installing-R-on-the-nodes


First a background point, I changed a line in mscript.sh from "export
Rex=$bin/R/bin/R-$RANDOM" to "export Rex=$bin/R/bin/R-$RANDOM$RANDOM".

Recent trouble shooting brought me to inspecting a temporary directory
created by Hadoop when you move an archive via a direct log in to a
node. This a working Hadoop install btw. It runs Hadoop benchmarks.
On my node this directory is:
/ln/hadoop_local_data/mapred/local/taskTracker/archive/
spicaRfolder.tar.gz/Rdist/R/bin


I noticed when I was in it that the contents were:

REMOVE

Rprof

Note: the accumulating renamed R executable. How far will that go?

This leads me to speculate at the bottom of mscript.R should be
something like:
"rm $Rex"

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: Accumulating random renamed R files
parts:
BTW is there a reason for the creation of a new file with a random
name other then the seding? If not try this as your mscript.sh. IMO
this is clearer and also doesn't depend on a sed statement that has to
be different for everyone.

The gist of the following script snippet is create all the
environmental variables that R does, set LD_LIBRARY_PATH, and jump
straight to the lines that R CMD invokes in the R script. Avoids
having to create new files.

##################### Works for me as mscript.sh
##################################

bin=`dirname "$0"`
RHIPE_HOME=`cd "$bin"; pwd`
export R_HOME=$RHIPE_HOME/R
export R_HOME_DIR=$R_HOME
export R_SHARE_DIR=$R_HOME/share
export R_INCLUDE_DIR=$R_HOME/include
export R_DOC_DIR=$R_HOME/doc
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$R_HOME/lib:$RHIPE_HOME
chmod -R 777 $RHIPE_HOME
. "${R_HOME}/etc${R_ARCH}/ldpaths"
exec sh $R_HOME/bin/Rcmd $RHIPE_HOME/imperious.so --slave --silent --
vanilla


#################### end mscript.sh
############################################
